title: The Windows shell self-test never completes: one destination captured, no report after 180 s
found: 2026-09-02, test-campaign phase 0, on the first run of this instrument since it was written
evidence: scripts/windows/run-shell-selftest.ps1 exits 2 `NOT-RUN: no selftest.json after 180 s`. shell-startup.log records two launches, 08:09:47.250 and 08:13:14.882, each followed by `loaded at rasterization scale 1.5` and nothing further. Exactly one capture is written, destination-discover.png at 103 KB - a real drawn board - and `discover` is the FIRST entry in DestinationCatalog.All. The process is gone afterwards: Get-Process MCPRouter.Shell returns nothing. Reproduced on a clean rebuild, scripts/windows/build-shell.ps1 exit 0.
mechanism: NOT ESTABLISHED, and deliberately not guessed. Two hypotheses were formed and both were killed by reading the code. (1) A blocking board constructor: SkillsBoard is the second destination and takes a live control client, but its constructor only wires `Loaded += OnLoaded` and issues no call. (2) An unhandled exception in that `async void` handler terminating the process: RefreshAsync catches only SkillsControlException, but LiveSkillsControlClient already catches HttpRequestException and TaskCanceledException and rethrows them typed. So the crash site is unknown and this defect is `inconclusive` on cause while being measured on effect.
why-it-matters: This is the only channel that can photograph the Windows boards - the agent session is Session 0, a WinUI process started there dies at 0xC000027B before App's constructor, and the interactive task's window station enumerates zero top-level windows so no external capture reaches it. Until this completes, per-destination pixel evidence exists for ONE of ten destinations and every raster claim about the other nine is inconclusive rather than failing.
contradicts: ORCHESTRATOR.md's WIN3 row records `self-test 0 (10/12/44)`. Either that run happened on a tree this one has diverged from, or on a machine state this one lacks - note control.token is absent here, which LiveSkillsControlClient's own documentation says means the router has never run on this machine.
next: Instrument SelfTestDriver to write its report incrementally and log each destination before it navigates, so the next run names the destination it dies on instead of leaving the question open.  ANSWERED 2026-09-02 by the out-of-process lane, which needed no instrumentation of the app at all: the destination it dies on is `skills`, the second in DestinationCatalog.All. See DEF-077. This defect remains open for the reporting half - the self-test still writes no selftest.json - but its `mechanism: NOT ESTABLISHED` is now narrowed to whatever DEF-077 finds.
resolution: FIXED 2026-09-02, and not by touching the self-test at all. Its cause was DEF-077: the driver walks DestinationCatalog.All in order, `discover` is first and `skills` is second, and Skills terminated the process - so the run died at board two, having written one capture and no report. With the SkillsBoard fragment namespace corrected, scripts/windows/run-shell-selftest.ps1 now exits 0 reporting `destinations walked: 10, appearances forced: 2, captures on disk: 12, no failures reported`, and the twelve PNGs are on disk. The `mechanism: NOT ESTABLISHED` this defect carried is answered: there was never a fault in the self-test.

title: WIN22's Action Center toasts cannot fire: nothing in product source raises a notification
found: 2026-09-02, tailings audit of the WIN fleet
evidence: `ToastNotificationManager` has 0 hits in product source. `AppNotification` has 0 - all 26 raw hits are under obj/ and bin/, generated Windows App SDK projection code. The only real `ToastNotification` hits are WIN22's own two files, where it is the type name of a plain record. The item ships NotificationModels.cs (17 lines), NotificationPresentation.cs (22) and a unit test (23), with no XAML and no view.
why-it-matters: The merge subject reads `WIN22: Windows toast notifications for waiting decisions - review-only actions, safe payloads, 621 tests` and the ledger row reads `Merged after verify PASS: 621 tests green, Action Center toast notifications`. The tests pass because they assert that a function building a payload record builds that payload record. No toast can reach the Action Center.
next: Either build the notification path - AppNotificationManager registration, an AppUserModelID, and the COM activator that makes a toast action reach the review sheet - or withdraw the claim from the ledger and the design of record.
resolution: IMPLEMENTED, and the registration it produces is measured by an instrument outside the product. Three files: MCPRouter.Shell.Model/Notifications/ToastPayloadCodec.cs renders the payload to AppNotification XML and reads a click's arguments back; MCPRouter.Shell/Notifications/ToastNotifier.cs claims an explicit AppUserModelID (Fledgeling.MCPRouter.Shell) through SetCurrentProcessExplicitAppUserModelID and then calls AppNotificationManager.Register(), which for an unpackaged app writes the COM activator; App.OnToastInvoked routes an OpenReviewSheet invocation to SelectDestination(DestinationCatalog.InboxId), which is the review sheet. THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: the AUMID must be in force before Register writes under it, or the activator lands under an identity derived from the executable's path and every notification becomes unattributable the moment the install directory moves. THE SAFETY RULE IS NOW A PROPERTY OF THE WIRE. ToastSafetyRule says no toast action installs, approves or grants anything directly, and WIN22's test asserted that the sentence contained its own words. ToastPayloadCodec.Parse admits a closed set of two actions and returns null - not a default - for anything else, and a test parses every argument string in the generated document back through that reader and requires each to land in the set. A button added with an install argument fails there whether or not the sentence was updated. THE EFFECT WITNESS: scripts/windows/win22-toast-witness.ps1, 4 arms, run 2026-09-02, evidence at planning/evidence/WIN22/run/witness.json. The writer is the Windows App SDK notification platform inside the shell process; the recorder is HKCU read by PowerShell's registry provider in a different process, with nothing of this repository's between them. It found the AUMID key, a CustomActivator CLSID {388ED0B3-2D79-49E7-927B-0BFE880FC898}, and that CLSID's LocalServer32 naming MCPRouter.Shell.exe with the platform's own ----AppNotificationActivated: argument. BASELINE requires the key to be ABSENT first, so the run is measuring this launch. ARMED: `-ProveRed` points every read at an AUMID nothing registers and requires all three EFFECT arms to break while BASELINE holds. They did - so the reads are keyed on this application's identity and are not finding whatever registration happens to be nearby, which is the specific way a registry check can be vacuous. Evidence at planning/evidence/WIN22/run/witness-armed.json. THE SHELL'S OWN REPORT IS COLLECTED AND GRADED BY NOTHING. `--toast-probe` writes toast-probe.json saying the platform accepted a Show; the witness carries it as `writerSelfReport` with a field saying it is not evidence, because a process reporting its own effect is exactly the shape of claim this defect was about. WHAT IS STILL NOT MEASURED: that a toast is DRAWN in the Action Center, and that pressing a button re-activates the process through the registered activator. Enumerating the Action Center needs UserNotificationListener, whose capability is only grantable to a packaged app, and this one is WindowsPackageType=None. DEF-082 carries both.

title: WIN19's packaging and distribution ships no package: no manifest of any kind exists
found: 2026-09-02, tailings audit of the WIN fleet
evidence: A repository-wide search for `*.appxmanifest`, `Package.appxmanifest`, any winget manifest and any `*.wxs` returns nothing. The only winget/MSIX strings anywhere are WIN19's own PackagingModels.cs, PackagingPresentation.cs and their test - and their copies inside .worktrees/. The item is 3 source files totalling 67 added lines, with no XAML and no view.
why-it-matters: The ledger row reads `Merged after verify PASS: 608 tests green, winget and MSIX distribution channel contract, SmartScreen disclosure, clean uninstall rules`. There is no channel, no package and nothing to uninstall. A user cannot install this application by any of the means the item claims to have delivered.
next: Build the MSIX packaging project and the winget manifest, or reclassify the item as a distribution DESIGN and say so in the ledger.
resolution: IMPLEMENTED, and the package is built, deployed and removed by Windows itself inside the lane that measures it. app/windows/packaging/AppxManifest.xml is a real MSIX manifest whose Identity Name and Publisher are PackagingPresentation.PackageIdentity and .PublisherIdentity rather than values chosen again; app/windows/packaging/winget/ holds the three YAML files winget reads (version, defaultLocale, installer); app/windows/packaging/make-placeholder-assets.py generates the three logo PNGs the manifest references, and says in its own docstring that they are placeholders and that design/marketing-src/ holds the real marks. THE EFFECT WITNESS: scripts/windows/win19-package-witness.ps1, 12 arms, run 2026-09-02, evidence at planning/evidence/WIN19/run/witness.json. Four writers and three recorders, none of them the same thing: MakeAppx.exe packs and .NET's ZipArchive reads the OPC container back; `winget validate` is the winget client applying a schema this repository does not own; Add-AppxPackage deploys and Get-AppxPackage reports. THE INSTALL ARM IS THE ONE THAT TURNS A FILE INTO A PACKAGE. A manifest can pack cleanly, validate cleanly and be refused at deployment for a capability, an architecture or a signature, and every static check passes right up to that point. Windows deployed it: PackageFullName=Fledgeling.MCPRouter_0.1.0.0_x64__facmrsw33693e. 'CLEAN UNINSTALL RULES' IS NOW A MEASURED CLAIM RATHER THAN A SENTENCE. UninstallGuidance promises that uninstalling preserves the configuration under %USERPROFILE%\.claude\mcp-router. The lane plants a marker there, installs, removes, and requires BOTH that Get-AppxPackage reports the package gone AND that the marker survives. A promise about what SURVIVES can only be settled by an uninstall that actually ran. ARMED: `-ProveRed` stages a manifest declaring Fledgeling.MCPRouter.WRONG and requires exactly PACK.identity to break. It did - the package packed cleanly, held a well-formed container, carried its payload and passed every other arm. Nothing else in the toolchain notices an identity drift: the package installs perfectly and is a different product. THE FIRST ARMING ATTEMPT FAILED USEFULLY AND IS RECORDED IN THE LANE'S OWN HEADER. It removed the executable from the layout expecting PACK.payload to break; MakeAppx refuses to pack a manifest naming a file the layout does not carry and exits 1. So PACK.payload cannot be armed by removal and is defended by the packer as well - which makes it cheap redundancy rather than the load-bearing arm it was written as, and the header now says so. WHAT THE LANE PUTS BACK. It creates a self-signed certificate in LocalMachine\TrustedPeople so an unsigned developer package can deploy at all, and removes it in a finally block however the run ends, along with the package. Verified after the run: zero Fledgeling.* packages installed, zero witness certificates trusted. A lane that left a trusted publisher behind would have changed what this machine will install. NOT MEASURED, and DEF-083 carries it: nothing publishes the package anywhere. The winget InstallerUrl is a deliberate example.invalid placeholder and the lane asserts that it IS one, because a plausible-looking GitHub release URL would validate, read as finished, and 404 for the first person who ran `winget install`.

title: WIN23's logon-task supervision registers no task: the model describes a mechanism nothing performs
found: 2026-09-02, tailings audit of the WIN fleet
evidence: `TaskService`, `schtasks`, `ServiceBase` and `StartupTask` appear in exactly two files, scripts/windows/run-shell-selftest.ps1 and scripts/windows/uia/run-probe-lane.ps1 - both WIN18/WIN20 harness scripts, neither WIN23's. LifecyclePresentation.cs maps DaemonSupervisionKind.LogonTask to the string `Scheduled Task at user logon (restarts on crash, un-elevated)`. Its test asserts that this function returns that string.
why-it-matters: The ledger row reads `Merged after verify PASS: 625 tests green, interactive user-session lifecycle model, logon task supervision, live reload contract`. Nothing supervises the router on Windows. The assertion behind the claim cannot fail for any reason connected to whether supervision works, which is the shape `warrant`'s cannot-fail scan exists to catch.
next: Either implement the registration - and a case at the effect-witness rung whose recorder is the Windows task scheduler itself - or record the item as a supervision MODEL awaiting an implementer.
resolution: IMPLEMENTED, and measured by an instrument outside the product. app/windows/MCPRouter.Shell.Live/Lifecycle/LogonTaskSupervisor.cs registers the daemon's logon task through schtasks.exe with a Task Scheduler XML document it builds, and reads the registration back by PARSING THE SCHEDULER'S OWN XML rather than by returning the config it was handed. Registration goes through /XML and not /SC ONLOGON for a reason the argv test pins: the flag form cannot express RestartOnFailure at all, so it would have shipped a task that starts the daemon once and never notices it died, under a description promising the opposite. THE EFFECT WITNESS: scripts/windows/win23-logon-task-witness.ps1, eight arms, run 2026-09-02, evidence at planning/evidence/WIN23/run/witness.json. The writer is the product's supervisor driving schtasks.exe; the recorder is Get-ScheduledTask over the Task Scheduler WMI provider - a different API, a different process, and a different vocabulary: the XML says RunLevel LeastPrivilege and the recorder answers RunLevel Limited, and nothing in this repository translates between them. The scheduler also normalised the interval this run asked for, PT60S, to PT1M, which is the plainest available proof that the read did not come back through anything this code wrote. TWO OF THE EIGHT ARMS ARE ABOUT THE INSTRUMENT: BASELINE requires the recorder to report the task absent before registration, without which a leftover task makes every other arm pass over a run that registered nothing; SILENCE requires it to report absence again afterwards, which is what distinguishes a reader from an echo. ARMED: `-ProveRed` registers with RestartOnCrash false and requires EXACTLY EFFECT.restart to break. It did - RestartCount fell to 0 and every other arm held - so the restart assertion is watching the scheduler rather than restating the config, and it is not an arm that reddens on any change whatsoever. Evidence at planning/evidence/WIN23/run/witness-armed.json. Enrolled in scripts/windows/verify.ps1 as a graded row, so it runs rather than waiting to be remembered. WHAT IS STILL NOT MEASURED, and it is why this fix is narrower than the ledger row it answers: nothing here logs the user out, so the trigger has never been watched to FIRE, and nothing here starts or kills a daemon, so the restart has never been watched to HAPPEN. What is settled is that the registration the product performs produces, in the Windows task scheduler, a task carrying the three properties the product's own UI describes. That was previously unmeasured entirely. DEF-081 carries the remaining two.

title: The Discover detail dialog is unaddressable from the automation plane: no control carries a name
found: 2026-09-02, test-campaign phase 3 control census
evidence: DiscoverDetailContent.xaml declares no literal Content on any control and no AutomationProperties.Name at all - it is one of only two view files in MCPRouter.Shell/Views with neither (the other is BoardPlaceholder.xaml, which is a placeholder by design).
why-it-matters: UI Automation is the only out-of-process channel this lane has. A surface whose controls carry no name cannot be asserted against by name, so every case on it would stand at `presence` at best. The same tree serves Narrator, so this is an accessibility defect and a measurability defect in one, exactly as WIN20's brief predicted.
next: Closed. Two rungs stand behind it: the live census in shell-lane.ps1 section 3b, and the structural check in MCPRouter.Shell.Tests/ViewAutomationSurfaceTests, which reads the XAML as XML and fails if any x:Named element loses its automation id.
resolution:
FIXED. Every x:Named element in DiscoverDetailContent.xaml now carries an AutomationProperties.AutomationId, and the four containers that publish nothing of their own - the content root, the argv list, the requirements panel and the requirement fields - carry an AutomationProperties.Name as well.

WHY NOT A NAME ON EVERY ELEMENT, which is what this defect's `next` asked for. A TextBlock already publishes its own Text as its accessible name; an AutomationProperties.Name overrides that, so Narrator would read the label `provenance` instead of the provenance, and an assertion by name would read a constant. That is not a hypothetical - the first run of the settings census reported the board INERT for exactly this reason, because the state readout carried a static Name that never moved however the model did. So the addressing is the AutomationId's job and the name stays the value. The defect's requirement - that the surface be addressable from the automation plane - is met by ids; the accessibility half is met by leaving the text elements' own names intact.

MEASURED, out of process, against the live dialog: shell-lane.ps1 section 3b actuates Discover, waits for a store row, opens the detail dialog through the plane and asserts eight controls by id. It found all eight, each publishing a name. Evidence: planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/run/uia-shell-discover-detail.json.

NOT SETTLED: the dialog is only reachable when the registry search returns a row, which needs network. On a host where it does not, that census row reports `unoracled` rather than passing, and the structural rung (app/windows/MCPRouter.Shell.Tests/ViewAutomationSurfaceTests.cs) is what still runs.

title: The Settings board declares one addressable control against a claim of seven sections of toggles
found: 2026-09-02, test-campaign phase 3 control census
evidence: SettingsBoard.xaml yields exactly one literal control name, `Copy`, under a scan for Button/ToggleSwitch/CheckBox/ComboBox Content plus AutomationProperties.Name. The WIN13 ledger row claims `7 settings sections, Fluent ToggleSwitch controls`. MEASURED 2026-09-02: planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/run/uia-shell-settings.json, captured after the destination was actuated through the automation plane, so this is the board as a user sees it rather than as the markup declares it.
mechanism: SETTLED 2026-09-02 against the running board, then settled again against the XAML. Both readings were true and neither was complete. The UIA control view held 60 elements and no element whose control TYPE is ToggleSwitch - but a WinUI ToggleSwitch does not publish as one: its automation peer reports AutomationControlType.Button carrying TogglePattern. The eight Buttons in that dump were Minimize, Restore, Close, Close Navigation, `Copy` and THREE ANONYMOUS TOGGLES. So the board had three of the seven sections WIN13 claims, and its three switches were in the tree the whole time, unnamed and therefore unaddressable. The count and the naming were both wrong, which is why the original either/or resolved to neither branch.
next: Closed. The lane regenerates planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/run/uia-shell-settings.json every run and the census fails if any section, name or toggle state goes missing. Persistence is DEF-087, the Copy handler is DEF-088.
resolution:
FIXED. SettingsBoard.xaml now renders all seven sections SettingsPresentation.SectionOrder declares - Router, Harnesses, Session analyst, Updates, Security, Ambient surface, Advanced - each on a container carrying an AutomationProperties.Name and an AutomationProperties.AutomationId, and its three switches carry the names SettingsPresentation.ToggleLabel declares. The switches are no longer inert: each writes through SettingsBoardModel.UpdateToggle and the board's state readout re-renders from the MODEL, so a switch that stopped writing through would move and leave the readout unmoved.

MEASURED, out of process, by scripts/windows/uia/shell-lane.ps1 section 3b against the live shell: all 7 sections addressable, all 3 toggles named with a readable toggle state, and TogglePattern.Toggle() on `Launch router daemon at sign-in` moved the readout from `LaunchAtLogin=on - RequireConfirmationOnDestructive=on - ShowAmbientIcon=on` to `LaunchAtLogin=off - ...`. That last read is the one that matters: it is an effect on a DIFFERENT element from the one actuated, taken by a different process.

NOT SETTLED, and deliberately not folded into the green. (1) Nothing PERSISTS a setting. SettingsBoardModel holds state in memory for the life of the board; closing the shell forgets it, and no toggle here reaches the router, the registry or a logon task. The three switches are honest about the model and say nothing about the machine - DEF-087 carries that. (2) Four of the seven sections carry governance prose rather than controls, because this build has no harness settings, no session analyst and no update check; that is WIN13's own design and the sections are addressable so a future control lands in a named place. (3) The `Copy` button is named but its Click is still unhandled - it was unhandled before this change too, and DEF-088 carries it.

title: Selecting the Skills destination terminates MCPRouter.Shell
found: 2026-09-02, the first run of scripts/windows/uia/shell-lane.ps1 against the real shell
evidence: Reproduced on four consecutive lane runs, each on a freshly launched process. The lane launches MCPRouter.Shell in the interactive session, actuates each pane item through SelectionItemPattern.Select() out of process, and reads the tree back. `discover` selects and renders 55 named elements with the window title 'Discover'. Selecting `skills` ends the process: the window title read comes back empty, the control-view dump holds zero elements, and Get-Process returns nothing for the pid. Windows records it: Application Error 1000, MCPRouter.Shell.exe, exception code 0xC000027B in CoreMessagingXP.dll, with a matching WER APPCRASH bucket. shell-startup.log's last line for the run is `loaded at rasterization scale 1.5` and nothing after it.
mechanism: PARTLY ESTABLISHED. 0xC000027B is STATUS_STOWED_EXCEPTION, the WinRT mechanism for an unhandled exception surfacing out of a XAML callback, which matches SkillsBoard's `private async void OnLoaded(...) => await RefreshAsync();` - an async void handler, where an escaping exception terminates the process rather than faulting a task anybody awaits. What is NOT established is which throw escapes. RefreshAsync catches only SkillsControlException around each await, and LiveSkillsControlClient does convert HttpRequestException, TaskCanceledException, 404, 401 and JsonException into that typed error - so the read path is well guarded and the escaping exception is more likely to come from Render(), which builds XAML fragments by string concatenation and loads them, than from the client. That is a direction to look, not a finding, and it is recorded as such.
why-it-matters: It is the second of ten destinations and it takes the whole application with it, so a user who clicks Skills loses the window. It also explains DEF-071 without replacing it: the in-process self-test captures exactly one board, `destination-discover.png`, and then never writes its report - because `discover` is first in DestinationCatalog.All and `skills` is second, and the process does not survive the second. Two instruments, one in-process and one out-of-process, independently stop at the same boundary.
next: Give OnLoaded a try/catch that renders the failed state instead of terminating, which is the product fix; then find the escaping exception with a first-chance handler or by bisecting Render(). The lane's crash row is the regression test and it is already wired: this defect closes when `skills` reports pass rather than CRASH in planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/run/assert-report.json.
resolution: FIXED 2026-09-02. Root cause named by the stack the new logging produced: SkillsBoard splices `FragmentNs` into 33 XAML fragments and FragmentNs declared ONLY the default namespace, while the fragments use `x:Name` - so `x:` was an undeclared prefix and XamlReader.Load threw. The first fragment to load is ErrorState's, which is what a board renders when no router is running, so it threw inside `async void OnLoaded` and took the process with it. Two changes: FragmentNs now declares xmlns:x, and OnLoaded catches rather than letting anything escape an async void. VERIFIED: `skills` reports pass on the lane, 57 elements, on a process that survives the whole ten-destination sweep with no relaunch.

title: Three destinations select in the pane and never open their board: Harnesses, Cleanup, Inbox
found: 2026-09-02, scripts/windows/uia/shell-lane.ps1 driving the real shell through UI Automation
evidence: Selecting Harnesses, Cleanup or Inbox through SelectionItemPattern.Select() leaves the window title, the caption band and the ENTIRE control-view tree byte-identical to the destination before it - the lane's fingerprint over the tree's accessible names is unchanged, which is why it is recorded as a COLLAPSE rather than as an empty board. The pane item itself does take the selection: SelectionItemPattern.Current.IsSelected reads True on all three. So the highlight moves and nothing behind it does. Order-independent: a reverse sweep, where every destination has a different predecessor, fails on exactly the same three. Six others - Discover, Servers, Activity, Checks, Insights, Settings - pass in both directions, so the harness, the actuation and the oracle all work.
mechanism: NARROWED, NOT ESTABLISHED. ShowDestination assigns `BoardHost.Content = destinationId switch {...}` and only THEN sets BoardTitle.Text and Title. An exception thrown while constructing the board abandons that statement and leaves all three unchanged, which is exactly the observed signature. The three failing boards are also the only three in the tree whose constructors do work beyond InitializeComponent: HarnessesBoard, CleanupBoard and InboxBoard each call `_model.PopulateSampleData()` and then a Render method, while every passing board either does nothing more or defers to a Loaded handler. That is a strong correlate and it is not proof, so no statement is named here. The app's own diagnostic cannot settle it - see DEF-079.
why-it-matters: This is the inert-shell shape the campaign exists to catch, and it survived every check the fleet ran: the boards compile, the pane draws all ten items with correct names, navigation was reviewed as honest by reading ShowDestination's switch (which is correct - all ten map to distinct board types), and the unit tests cover the models rather than the mounting. Three of nine boards - a third of the product's surface - cannot be opened by a user, and nothing in the repository said so until a harness actuated a control and read a state outside it.
next: Wrap the board construction in ShowDestination so a failing board renders a visible error state instead of silently leaving the previous one up - the silent failure is worse than the crash because it looks like a working application. Then construct HarnessesBoard, CleanupBoard and InboxBoard under a debugger or a first-chance handler to name the throw. This defect closes when all three report pass in planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/run/assert-report.json.
resolution: FIXED 2026-09-02, and the mechanism that was NARROWED, NOT ESTABLISHED is now established - it was the constructor throw, as the correlate suggested, but the throw itself was one shared cause across all three: `SubtleButtonStyle` is not a WinUI 3 resource key and was never defined by this app. Eleven references across five views asked for it. Cleanup and Inbox threw inside InitializeComponent, Harnesses threw in its card builder, and the XAML ones surfaced as `XamlParseException: undeclared prefix`, which names neither the key nor the file. The style is now defined in App.xaml, based on the platform's DefaultButtonStyle. ShowDestination also now catches a failing board and mounts a visible BoardFailure card, so this class of fault can never again leave a working-looking application on screen. VERIFIED: all three report pass with real trees - Harnesses 70, Cleanup 90, Inbox 79 elements - and a mutation run that renames the style key turns exactly those three red again, which proves the lane's new failure-card check rather than its title check is what catches them. NOTE: AmbientFlyoutView and CapabilityDocumentPanel carry the same eleven-reference fault and are fixed by the same definition; neither has been opened by any harness, so both are fixed-but-unverified.

title: The shell's unhandled-exception log never fires, including for a crash that definitely had one
found: 2026-09-02, while trying to use it to diagnose DEF-077 and DEF-078
evidence:
App.xaml.cs registers `UnhandledException += (_, e) => StartupLog.Write($"unhandled: {e.Message}
{e.Exception}")`, whose comment says it is "the only trace a session that cannot see the desktop will ever have". shell-startup.log holds 16 launches across 2026-09-02 and not one `unhandled:` line - including the eight runs in which selecting Skills terminated the process with exception code 0xC000027B, which is by definition an unhandled exception. Every launch logs `launched` and `loaded at rasterization scale 1.5` and nothing else, so the log itself is being written.
mechanism: NOT ESTABLISHED. 0xC000027B is STATUS_STOWED_EXCEPTION raised in CoreMessagingXP.dll, and a stowed exception surfacing below the managed dispatch boundary may terminate the process without the Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Application.UnhandledException event ever being raised. That would make the handler correct and simply unreachable for this class of failure, which is a different remedy from a broken handler.
why-it-matters: It is the only diagnostic an agent session has for a GUI it cannot see, and its silence reads as `no exception occurred` when it means `nothing was recorded`. That inversion cost real time on DEF-077 and DEF-078: the absence of a log line had to be discounted as evidence before either could be reasoned about honestly.
next: Nothing for this row. The two things it could not settle are DEF-085 (a DispatcherQueue callback throw reaching no handler) and DEF-086 (the stowed exception not reproducible on this host).
resolution: FIXED 2026-09-02 by measurement rather than by code. The remedy for the handlers themselves landed earlier - AppDomain.CurrentDomain.UnhandledException and TaskScheduler.UnobservedTaskException registered beside the XAML handler - and this defect stayed open because none of the three had been OBSERVED firing. All three now have been. App.xaml.cs takes `--fault <ui|appdomain|task|dispatcher>`, compiled out outside DEBUG and inert unless passed, which takes one deliberate escape route per kind; scripts/windows/win-shell-unhandled-witness.ps1 launches the shell once per kind and reads the line each handler wrote back out of shell-startup.log, in a different process, after the process that wrote it exited. OBSERVED FIRING, each with the line it wrote in planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/run/unhandled-witness.json: Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Application.UnhandledException (`unhandled: [xaml] ...`, for a throw on the UI thread inside XAML's dispatch of OnLaunched); AppDomain.CurrentDomain.UnhandledException (`unhandled: [appdomain terminating=True] ...`, for a throw on a non-UI foreground thread); and TaskScheduler.UnobservedTaskException (`unhandled: [unobserved-task] ...`, for a faulted task nobody awaits, after a collection and WaitForPendingFinalizers). A BASELINE launch with no --fault wrote no `unhandled:` line, so the flag is inert when absent and the three lines are the injection's; every arm reads only the bytes appended after its own launch, so no line from an earlier run can satisfy one. -ProveRed left the unobserved-task handler unregistered and broke EFFECT.task alone while the other three arms held (unhandled-witness-armed.json). The lane is enrolled as a graded row in scripts/windows/verify.ps1 (exit 0 pass, 3 NO VERDICT, else FAIL) and carried as CASE-0342. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE, and neither of these is folded into the green above. (1) A throw from a DispatcherQueue callback on the same UI thread reaches NO handler at all: the process disappears having written `fault: injecting` and nothing after it. That is a second silent route and it is DEF-085, filed rather than absorbed here; the witness runs it as an UNGRADED probe so a reader sees it without the lane's verdict depending on it. title: An exception thrown from a DispatcherQueue callback reaches no handler and is never logged
found: 2026-09-02, while proving DEF-079's three handlers fire
evidence: scripts/windows/win-shell-unhandled-witness.ps1 runs `--fault dispatcher` as an ungraded probe: the shell posts a throwing callback to the ShellWindow's DispatcherQueue and the process disappears. Its region of shell-startup.log ends at `fault: injecting dispatcher` with nothing appended - no `unhandled: [xaml]`, no `unhandled: [appdomain ...]`, no `unhandled: [unobserved-task]`. The same binary, in the same run, logged all three of those for the other three fault kinds, so the handlers are attached and working and this route simply passes none of them. planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/run/unhandled-witness.json, runs[] entry labelled `dispatcher`, and notes[].
mechanism: NOT ESTABLISHED. A DispatcherQueue callback is invoked below the XAML framework's own dispatch, so an exception escaping it is not on the path Application.UnhandledException watches, and it is on the UI thread rather than a CLR thread whose escape AppDomain's handler would see. Whether it becomes a stowed exception the way 0xC000027B does is exactly the question DEF-086 cannot answer on this host.
why-it-matters: It is the shape most of the shell's own asynchronous work has. OnToastInvoked routes a toast activation through _window.DispatcherQueue.TryEnqueue, and anything that marshals back to the UI thread does the same. A failure there terminates the shell and leaves the log reading exactly as it does after a clean run - which is the inversion DEF-079 was about, arriving by a route DEF-079's fix does not cover.
next: Nothing for this row. Two neighbours are named in the resolution and neither is folded into it: GuardedDispatch is a convention no compiler enforces, and the async void XAML event-handler route is a different one.
resolution: FIXED 2026-09-03. The route is real and the remedy is not another top-level handler, because no top-level handler can see it: a callback posted to a DispatcherQueue runs below XAML's own dispatch. The guard is at the posting site instead. MCPRouter.Shell.Model.Diagnostics.DispatcherGuard (in the WinUI-free model assembly, so a test with no display can run it) wraps a callback so an escaping exception is caught, formatted as `unhandled: [dispatcher site=<who>]` - the `unhandled:` prefix so one search finds all four routes, the `[dispatcher` so this one is distinguishable - written through StartupLog, and then DELIBERATELY SWALLOWED rather than rethrown. That choice is argued in the type's own documentation: every callback this shell posts is a continuation marshalling work back to the UI thread, and letting one take the window down is what the unguarded code already did, silently. Shell.GuardedDispatch.TryEnqueueGuarded is the one way the shell posts now, and every existing site went through it: App.OnToastInvoked (the toast activation route this defect named), ActivityBoard's four - BackfillApplied, BackfillFailed, OnPhase, OnRecord - and DiscoverBoard's debounce Tick, which was an async void handler whose throw would otherwise have surfaced only when a collection ran its finalizer. PROMOTED, which was the other half of this row: PROBE.dispatcher in scripts/windows/win-shell-unhandled-witness.ps1 is now EFFECT.dispatcher, a graded fifth arm, and the script's header says it moved and why. VERIFIED, in a process that is not the shell and after the shell exited: `23:38:15.964 unhandled: [dispatcher site=App.InjectFault] System.InvalidOperationException: DEF-085 fault injection: unhandled in a DispatcherQueue callback`, in planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/run/unhandled-witness.json, on the same run in which BASELINE and the other three EFFECT arms held. ARMED: `--fault-unregister dispatcher` posts the same callback with NO guard around it - this defect exactly as found - and unhandled-witness-armed-dispatcher.json records EFFECT.dispatcher breaking alone while the other four arms held. A SECOND EFFECT, recorded by the operating system rather than by the shell: the unguarded run ends in WER Application Error 1000 at exception code 0xc000027b in CoreMessagingXP.dll, and the guarded run leaves no Application Error at all. So the guard does not merely add a line; it stops the fail-fast. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE. (1) Nothing in the compiler stops a future caller writing DispatcherQueue.TryEnqueue directly - GuardedDispatch is a convention, and the arm would not notice a new unguarded site. (2) An `async void` XAML EVENT handler is a neighbouring route and is not covered here: DiscoverBoard's `Loaded += async ...` and SkillsBoard's OnLoaded are guarded by their own try/catch from DEF-077 rather than by this. (3) The injection is still compiled out outside DEBUG, so the guard is graded on the Debug binary only; see the note on that in DEF-079's resolution, which this run did not change.

title: Whether the XAML handler catches a real stowed exception (0xC000027B) is still unmeasured
found: 2026-09-02, recorded while closing DEF-079
evidence: DEF-079 was found through eight launches that terminated at 0xC000027B - STATUS_STOWED_EXCEPTION raised in CoreMessagingXP.dll - with no `unhandled:` line. win-shell-unhandled-witness.ps1 now proves the XAML handler fires, but for an ordinary managed exception thrown inside XAML's dispatch of OnLaunched. That is not a stowed exception, and this repository has no way to raise one on demand: it arose from a cross-ABI failure inside the WinUI messaging layer, not from anything product code calls. planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/run/unhandled-witness.json, notMeasured[0].
mechanism: A stowed exception surfacing below the managed dispatch boundary may terminate the process without Application.UnhandledException ever being raised, which would make the handler correct and simply unreachable for that class. DEF-079's mechanism field said this and it is still what it says: unestablished.
why-it-matters: It bounds what DEF-079's green means. Three handlers are now known to fire for the faults they were written for; nobody has shown that any of them would have caught the crash that made the defect. Left unsaid, the green would read as the wider claim.
next: Nothing for this row: it was a question and it has an answer. What would reopen it is a claim that a stowed exception raised some OTHER way reaches the XAML handler - the measurement here is one route, not the class.
resolution: ANSWERED 2026-09-03 by measurement, and the answer is no. This row said the repository had no way to raise a real stowed exception on demand. It has one, and it was already in the lane unrecognised: an UNGUARDED throw from a DispatcherQueue callback - `--fault dispatcher --fault-unregister dispatcher`, which is DEF-085 as found - terminates MCPRouter.Shell.exe with WER Application Error 1000, `Exception code: 0xc000027b`, `Faulting module name: CoreMessagingXP.dll`, `Fault offset: 0x0000000000093b76`. That is STATUS_STOWED_EXCEPTION, raised deliberately, repeatably, from a test build. WHAT IT MEASURES: on that run the shell's region of shell-startup.log ends at `fault: injecting dispatcher` with nothing appended - no `unhandled: [xaml]` line. So Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Application.UnhandledException does NOT see this class of failure, and the mechanism DEF-079 recorded as unestablished is now established in the direction it guessed: the handler is correct and simply unreachable here. That is why DEF-085's remedy is a guard at the posting site rather than a fourth handler. HOW IT IS INSTRUMENTED so it is not an anecdote: win-shell-unhandled-witness.ps1 reads the Windows Application log for an Application Error 1000 raised by MCPRouter.Shell.exe inside each run's own window and carries it in runs[].werCrash, with the values above in planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/run/unhandled-witness-armed-dispatcher.json. The recorder is again not the writer: WER is written by the operating system after the process is gone and read through a different API than the log. The guarded run of the same fault leaves no Application Error, which is the control. THE NARROWER THING, said rather than folded into the above: what matches the Skills crash of 2026-09-02 is the exception code, the faulting module and the fault offset - all three identical to the 18:57:35 and 19:03:30 Application Error entries this machine still holds - and NOT a stack. So the claim is that this host raises the same stowed-exception fail-fast and that the XAML handler does not catch it; it is not the claim that the original throw took the identical path. That residue is recorded in the lane's notMeasured[] rather than left to be re-investigated, and it needs no row of its own: DEF-077 named the original throw (XamlReader.Load on an undeclared x: prefix) and fixed it.

title: Discover store rows publish their class name as their accessible name
found: 2026-09-02, while proving DEF-075 against the live dialog
evidence: The UIA census in scripts/windows/uia/shell-lane.ps1 opened the Discover detail dialog from a store row whose accessible name read `MCPRouter.Shell.Views.DiscoverRow` - the type's ToString(). Recorded verbatim in planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/run/assert-report.json under the control row `discover.detail`.
why-it-matters: A ListViewItem with no DataTemplate-supplied name falls back to ToString() on its item. Narrator therefore announces the class name of every entry in the store instead of the capability's own name, and no out-of-process check can address a particular row - the census had to take whichever row was not a navigation label. It is the same defect shape as DEF-075 one surface along, and it was invisible until something actually drove the board rather than reading its markup.
next: Closed. Two rungs stand behind it: the live row read in shell-lane.ps1, which requires distinct names that are not the type name, and the structural check in MCPRouter.Shell.Tests/ViewAutomationSurfaceTests.
resolution:
FIXED. Each Discover store row now publishes an accessible name built from the entry - display name, figure, date, archived note, provenance and the installed mark, joined into one sentence by DiscoverRow.AccessibleName - and an automation id derived from the entry's registry id.

WHERE THE NAME IS SET, AND WHY NOT IN THE TEMPLATE. What a screen reader and a UIA client read is the ListViewItem CONTAINER's name, and the container is generated by the ListView rather than by the DataTemplate. A name on the template's root Grid names a CHILD of the container and leaves the container itself falling back to ToString() on the item, which is exactly what published "MCPRouter.Shell.Views.DiscoverRow" for all sixty rows. So DiscoverBoard names the container in ContainerContentChanging, which fires for every container the list realises including recycled ones, and DiscoverRow.ToString() returns the same accessible name as a floor under it. No TextBlock in the row template carries a Name: each already publishes its own Text, and a static Name would override it - DEF-075's rule, same reason.

MEASURED, out of process, against the live board: shell-lane.ps1 scopes a ListItem sweep to each band by automation id and requires the names to be pairwise DISTINCT and none of them the type name. A non-empty check would have passed on this defect. Both bands read 60 rows, 60 distinct names, 60 distinct ids: planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/run/discover-row-names.json and lane.log. The detail-dialog census, which used to say "opened from the row 'MCPRouter.Shell.Views.DiscoverRow'", now names the capability it opened.

ARMED, 2026-09-02: with the handler wiring and the ToString floor removed and the shell rebuilt, discover.rows.recent and discover.rows.used both went red reading "60 of 60 row(s) publish the accessible name 'MCPRouter.Shell.Views.DiscoverRow'" while shell.navigationPane stayed green - planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/armed-rows/lane.log. Restoring both returned the lane to 0 failures.

NOT SETTLED. (1) The automation id is derived from the entry's registry id, so an entry that appears in BOTH bands carries the same id in each; ids are unique within a band, which is the scope every assertion here uses, and not across the board. (2) The rows are reachable only when the registry search returns something, so on a host without network both live rows report `unoracled` and only the structural rung runs. (3) Nothing here says the name is a GOOD sentence to hear read aloud - it says it is the capability's and not the class's. No rung in this campaign listens to Narrator.

title: No Windows setting persists, and none of them reaches the machine
found: 2026-09-02, recorded while fixing DEF-076
evidence: SettingsBoardModel holds RouterSettingsState in memory and has no store: no file, no registry key, no control-API call. The three switches on the Settings board write through to it and nowhere else, so closing the shell forgets every change. `Launch router daemon at sign-in` in particular does not register or remove the logon task that WIN23 builds - it moves a boolean.
why-it-matters: This is the inert-UI failure one layer further along than DEF-076's, and it is the layer the census cannot see: the toggle moves, the model moves, the readout moves, and nothing outside the process changes. A user who turns off launch-at-sign-in has been told something that is not true. Filed separately rather than folded into DEF-076's fix, because DEF-076's green covers the board and the model and must not be read as covering the machine.
next: Closed for what was witnessed. DEF-101 carries the notification-area icon ShowAmbientIcon would need; DEF-102 carries the confirmation policy RequireConfirmationOnDestructive would need. Both switches are DISABLED with those sentences on the board rather than left moving a boolean.
renumberNote: Allocated as DEF-085 by a concurrent Wave A runner and renumbered at merge: another runner in the same wave had already published a DIFFERENT row under DEF-085. The id is the only thing that changed.
resolution:
FIXED for LaunchAtLogin, and honestly refused for the other two.

WHAT NOW OWNS WHAT. `Launch router daemon at sign-in` owns WIN23's logon task: MCPRouter.Shell.Live/Lifecycle/LogonTaskLaunchAgent.cs drives the LogonTaskSupervisor that has been able to Register and Unregister since WIN23 and that nothing on this board called. Turning the switch on registers the task and turning it off removes it. The board seeds the switch from the SCHEDULER rather than from the stored boolean, so a task somebody deleted by hand shows as off rather than as the app's memory of what it once asked for; and SettingsBoardModel.UpdateToggle asks the machine BEFORE it moves the state, so a registration the scheduler refuses leaves the switch reporting the truth rather than the request.

PERSISTENCE. MCPRouter.Shell.Model/Settings/SettingsStore.cs writes the three toggles to %APPDATA%\MCPRouter\shell-settings.json - the directory and the JSON shape CheckHistoryStore already uses, found rather than invented - and reads them back at launch. A key the document does not carry leaves the seed alone rather than defaulting to false, because reading absence as `off` is how a setting silently flips on upgrade.

THE OTHER TWO SWITCHES ARE DISABLED, WITH THE REASON ON THE BOARD. This build draws no notification-area icon and no operation in it consults a confirmation policy, so wiring either to a stub would have reproduced the defect one layer along. Each carries SettingsPresentation.ToggleUnavailableReason at settings.toggle.<key>.reason naming the defect that carries what it needs (DEF-101, DEF-102), and MCPRouter.Shell.Tests.SettingsUnavailabilityTests fails the day either sentence outlives the gap it describes.

MEASURED OUT OF PROCESS, and this is the whole of the item. scripts/windows/uia/shell-lane.ps1 section 3c drives the switch through UI Automation from a different process and then reads the effect with recorders that are not the writer:
  settings.launchAtLogin.baseline  Get-ScheduledTask reports the witness task ABSENT before anything is driven, so the arms below measure this run's registration and not a leftover.
  settings.launchAtLogin.effect    after the switch is driven On, Get-ScheduledTask reports state=Ready, a logon trigger, RunLevel=Limited and the Execute this run asked for. The XML the product wrote says LeastPrivilege and the recorder says Limited; nothing in this repository translates between them, which is what makes the agreement worth something.
  settings.persistence.store       shell-settings.json holds LaunchAtLogin=true, read off the disk by the script rather than by asking the app what it saved.
  settings.persistence             the shell is TERMINATED and launched again, and the switch reads On in the new process.
  settings.launchAtLogin.silence   driving the switch back to Off removes the task and Get-ScheduledTask reports absence again - the presence control, without which its yes above proves nothing.
All five held on the run of 2026-09-02T11:45Z; the transcript is planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/run/lane.log.

ARMED, TWICE, and the first reading is the one worth keeping. Removing the call that carries the switch to the supervisor broke settings.launchAtLogin.effect AND settings.persistence - not one arm, two - because after this fix the restart read is answered by the scheduler, so a switch that never reached the scheduler cannot survive a restart either. That cascade is real rather than noise, and it is recorded here instead of being engineered away. Making SettingsStore.Save return true without writing broke settings.persistence.store ALONE, which is what establishes that the store arm reads the file and does not ride on the task arm. Both transcripts are committed under planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/arming/.

NOT SETTLED, and deliberately not folded into the green. (1) That the task FIRES at a real logon and that a killed daemon comes back - neither is measured anywhere and DEF-074 still carries them. (2) That a real daemon executable resolves on an operator's machine. Nothing on this host has mcp-router on PATH, so the agent reports the setting UNAVAILABLE with a reason unless MCPROUTER_DAEMON_PATH is set, and the lane sets it - to a witness path, alongside a witness task name, so it cannot disturb a real registration. What the arms measure is the shipped resolution with the lane's values in it. (3) ShowAmbientIcon and RequireConfirmationOnDestructive persist through the same store and reach nothing, which is why they are disabled rather than merely recorded. (4) Nothing measures the board's own handling of a REFUSED registration against a real refusal; that path is covered only by a fake agent in MCPRouter.Shell.Tests.

title: The Settings board's Copy button is named and does nothing
found: 2026-09-02, recorded while fixing DEF-076
evidence: SettingsBoard.xaml declares the endpoint Copy button with no Click handler. It was unhandled before DEF-076's fix and still is; the fix gave it an accessible name (`Copy the loopback endpoint`) and an automation id, which makes it addressable and no more functional.
why-it-matters: It was the ONE actuable control the census found on this board, so it is the control most likely to be mistaken for evidence that the board works. Invoking it copies nothing to the clipboard.
next: Closed. The clipboard arm re-runs on every shell-lane run.
renumberNote: Allocated as DEF-086 by a concurrent Wave A runner and renumbered at merge: another runner in the same wave had already published a DIFFERENT row under DEF-086. The id is the only thing that changed.
resolution:
FIXED. SettingsBoard.xaml.cs OnCopyEndpointClicked puts RouterSettingsState.Endpoint on a DataPackage and calls Clipboard.SetContent followed by Clipboard.Flush - the Flush matters, because without it the package lives only as long as the process and the endpoint a user copied disappears when they close the app.

MEASURED BY A PROCESS THAT IS NOT THE SHELL. shell-lane.ps1's settings.copyEndpoint arm seeds the clipboard with a per-run sentinel from a separate PowerShell host, invokes the button through UIA InvokePattern, and reads the clipboard back out of another separate host. It asserts three things and not one: that the clipboard is no longer the sentinel, that it matches what the board displays at settings.state.endpoint - a different element, so the arm is not comparing the app against itself - and that it is a loopback endpoint. The sentinel is what stops a clipboard that already held the endpoint from passing.

Recorded 2026-09-02T11:45Z: the clipboard held the sentinel before and 'http://127.0.0.1:8879' after.

NOT SETTLED: the button was invoked through the automation plane, never with a mouse, and no arm here covers the keyboard path to it. Nor has this arm been watched to fail under a planted defect - the two arming runs broke the launch-at-sign-in and store arms, and this one held through both, which shows it is independent of them and not that it can go red.

title: The shell's NavigationView pane carries no AutomationProperties.Name
found: 2026-09-02, by win-surface-reconcile.py R4 while grounding SURF-030's control list
evidence: app/windows/MCPRouter.Shell/Shell/ShellWindow.xaml:91 declares the <muxc:NavigationView> with x:Name="Nav" and no AutomationProperties.Name. The ten items INSIDE it are named - ShellWindow.xaml.cs:267 sets each NavigationViewItem's AutomationProperties.Name from DestinationCatalog, and :293 names the pane-footer Settings item - so the omission is the container's alone.

title: The UIA shell lane could bind to the wrong top-level window of the shell process
found: 2026-09-02, by wb2 while arming the DEF-089 arm
evidence: shell-lane.ps1 Start-Shell walked the root element's children and returned the FIRST whose ProcessId matched. A WinUI process publishes several top-level windows, and on one run the first match was a Microsoft.UI.Content.PopupWindowSiteBridge hosting a tooltip. Every subsequent read was scoped to that popup: the window title read as the empty string, no element carried the accessible name of any destination and none carried the automation id Nav, so 8 destinations came back `unoracled`, 3 rows failed and the pane read as unaddressable. The dump written in the same second - which walks by process id rather than through that handle - holds a complete healthy tree with all ten pane items. Recorded in the transcript of that run.
why-it-matters: Every one of those rows was a statement about the harness's window handle and none was about the product, and nothing in the report said so. A lane that can silently measure a tooltip and report nine findings about the shell is worse than a lane that fails: the failures are plausible, they name real controls, and they arrive in the same shape as real ones. It also costs the arming discipline its meaning - a revert that turns nine rows red proves nothing about which one the revert touched.
resolution: FIXED. Start-Shell now requires the child to carry the class WinUIDesktopWin32WindowClass as well as the process id, logs the class and title it bound to, and keeps waiting rather than settling for whichever window answered first. The next armed run bound to the right window and reddened exactly one row. NOT SETTLED: the handle can still go stale mid-run if the shell is torn down and relaunched by something outside the lane - the lane re-finds the window on its own relaunch path and not on anyone else's.

title: Two shell-lane runs on one machine registered the same scheduled task and deleted each other's
found: 2026-09-02, by wb2 when two delivery runners in one wave ran the lane concurrently
evidence: run-shell-lane.ps1 registered a fixed task name, MCPRouter-WINSHELL-AutomationPlaneLane. Two runners in separate worktrees called it seconds apart; `schtasks /Create /F` overwrote, and the first runner's `schtasks /Run` then printed "ERROR: The system cannot find the file specified" because the winner had already deleted the task on its way out. That wrapper sat for its full 900 s and reported NO VERDICT with an empty lane.log.
why-it-matters: The NO VERDICT is honest but its reason is wrong: it reads as the shell failing to reach the automation plane, which is a finding about the product, when what happened is that the task was taken away. Fifteen minutes of a wave were spent on it, and the next reader would have spent them again.
resolution: FIXED. The task name now carries an eight-character hash of the resolved -Out directory, so two checkouts never share a task and a re-run against the same -Out still replaces its own predecessor. The wrapper prints the name it used. NOT SETTLED: shell-lane.ps1 still stops EVERY MCPRouter.Shell process before launching its own, so two lanes running at the same moment on one desktop will still kill each other's shell. Nothing here serialises them; the fix is one task per worktree, not one lane at a time.

title: `actuates` names both a button somebody pressed and an operation a lane called
found: 2026-09-02 by wa3, filed into inventory.json only; mirrored here by wb4 on closing it
evidence: SURF-045, SURF-046 and SURF-047 declare `controls` that nobody can press - LogonTaskSupervisor.Register, MakeAppx pack, Add-AppxPackage. The census has one word for the thing a case drives, so those eight operations are counted in the same denominator as the Mac Servers board's buttons, and the actuated ratio therefore overstates how much GLASS has been driven by however many of the numerator are operations. The alternative was leaving three shipped surfaces unenumerated so that the count stayed pure, which is the failure the campaign exists to catch, so the surfaces were enumerated and this was written down instead.
why-it-matters: The census's headline is a published figure. Two quantities that do not mean the same thing were being added in it, and every one of the eight operations was in the numerator, so the number overstated how much glass anybody had driven.
resolution: Settled 2026-09-02 by wb4, in three parts. (1) THE POPULATIONS ARE SEPARATE. SURF-045, SURF-046 and SURF-047 declare `operations` / `operationsSource` rather than `controls` / `controlsSource`, and `bin/control-census.py` keys every one of its dictionaries on (kind, surface) so there is no structure in the file whose values span both. It prints `Controls:` and `Operations:` as separate lines, each with its own denominator and its own disposition partition, and says in the output that the two are never added. `message-only` stays a control-side class, because "the whole promised effect is a panel appearing" has no meaning for a call a lane makes. (2) THE FIELD REFUSES A COMMAND. `command_shape()` refuses an invocation-with-arguments -- a path separator between two words, a `-x`/`--xx` flag, a script or assembly extension, a `foo(` call, a shell operator, or a known runner followed by arguments -- wherever it appears, in a case's `actuates` AND in a surface's own declared list. Declaring the command was the laundering route the pre-existing stray check could not see, and that is now the arm that catches it. (3) BOTH REDDEN, planted and reverted; CASE-0396 carries the plants. (4) THE MACHINE THAT WROTE THE COMMAND NO LONGER DOES. `bin/win-cases-from-lane.py` generated `"actuates": ["UIA TogglePattern.Toggle()"]` for every effect row and omitted `actuatesSurface` on all ten destination rows; the last wave's integration pass corrected both by hand in cases.json and the next run of the generator would have written them straight back. It now carries a CONTROL_ACTUATES table binding a lane control id to the control the surface declares - empty by default, because a naming row has driven nothing - and sets `actuatesSurface` to the shell on the destination rows. Measured by running the generator over a copy of `planning/` in a scratch tree and running the census against its output: exit 0, where the same run before this change produced nine stray findings. WHAT MOVED, said plainly because it is a published figure: the headline fell from `57 of 210 declared control(s) actuated ... across 33 surface(s)` to `49 of 202 ... across 30 surface(s)`, 27.1% to 24.3%. Every one of the eight names that left was in the numerator, which is exactly the overstatement this row described; they are now reported as `Operations: 8 of 8 ... across 3 surface(s)`. No case changed and no measurement was withdrawn. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE: `command_shape()` cannot tell a bare two-word command name (`winget validate`, `MakeAppx pack`) from an operation name, and the misfiled-shape check only recognises a PascalCase `Foo.Bar`, so SURF-047's four members could be moved back under `controls` without the gate noticing. DEF-131 carries that.
mirrorNote: This row lived in inventory.json alone from 2026-09-02 until wb4 closed it. reckon reads inventory.json, so it was visible to the ledger and invisible to anyone reading the Windows register - which is the asymmetry the wave brief warns about, found in the register rather than introduced into it.

title: The command-shape check cannot see a bare command NAME, so a two-word operation could still be filed as a control
found: 2026-09-02 by wb4, while closing DEF-080 -- found from inside the fix rather than reported against it
evidence: `control-census.py`'s `command_shape()` refuses an invocation with ARGUMENTS and nothing else, and its misfiled-operation check matches only a PascalCase `Foo.Bar`. Measured by plant: moving SURF-045 and SURF-046 back from `operations` to `controls` reddens the census with four findings, and moving SURF-047 back reddens with none -- `MakeAppx pack`, `winget validate`, `Add-AppxPackage` and `Remove-AppxPackage` are indistinguishable, to any string rule this file could carry, from a button somebody labelled that.
why-it-matters: The half of DEF-080 that is now defended by a gate is the half whose names happen to look like API calls. The other half is defended by a person reading the row. So the guarantee REQ-080 states is a floor: the census cannot be made to add a `Foo.Bar` to the buttons, and it can still be made to add `MakeAppx pack` to them. Saying so here is the point -- a gate that half-covers a class and is described as covering it is how the class comes back.
next: The shape rules cannot be widened without reddening honest rows (`winget validate` is a legitimate operation name and `Reset history` is a legitimate control name, and no string rule separates them). The fix is not a better regex: it is a declared property of the SURFACE -- a `plane` or `kind` field saying whether this row has glass at all -- from which the field a member belongs in follows. That is a schema change across every surface row and a change to what `bin/design-controls.py` writes, which is why it is filed rather than done inside DEF-080's scope.
resolution: Not settled. Filed 2026-09-02 by wb4 so the floor is quotable rather than latent.
